subject: Pricing & context profiling — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.dev>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fintechsolutions.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus@fintechsolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.dev>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 19:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & context profiling - post-demo recap

Hi Alyssa / Marcus,

Thanks for taking the time today — really appreciated the demo and the clear use-case walkthrough. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can turn this into a concrete pilot proposal: 

1) High-level profile we captured on the call (please correct me if I mis-stated anything):
   - Primary workload: monthly statement generation + interactive customer support snippets.
   - Expected initial traffic: roughly 10-12k generation requests/day across both flows.
   - Context mix: ~70% short-context (<=8k), ~25% mid-context (32k), ~5% long-context (128k) for large statement merges and full-account histories.
   - Typical sizes (ballpark): avg prompt tokens ~1.2k, avg completion tokens ~850 for the support flow; for statement generation prompts average ~3k prompt / ~6k completion.

2) Pricing/target economics you mentioned on the call: target pricing in the range $10-15 per 1M tokens for typical 8k workloads, and willingness to consider uplift for 32k/128k if the unit economics are transparent.

3) Action items from our side:
   - I will draft a mutual action plan (MAP) and a preliminary pricing slab reflecting the context-length differentials (8k vs 32k vs 128k).
   - We need a small sample of typical payloads (anonymized or redacted) so we can run tokenization and vet caching opportunities.
   - Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra lead to confirm retention, KV cache expectations, and quantization recommendations.

Attachments: I will include a first-pass MAP and a customer data profile template for you to fill in; those will include the fields we typically need to estimate unit cost accurately.

Next steps: If you can share 2-3 representative payloads and a rough monthly volume split (support vs statements vs embeddings) by EOD Thursday, I will turn around a priced pilot proposal by Friday.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.dev | +1 415-555-0192

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fintechsolutions.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.dev>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus@fintechsolutions.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 07:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & context profiling - post-demo recap

Connor, thanks, this is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

- Volumes: we expect a phased ramp: month 1: ~1.2M prompt tokens / ~2.8M completion tokens; month 3: ~4M prompt / ~9M completion as we onboard two additional product lines.
- Profile detail: for the statement generation pipeline (the heavy context flow) prompts average ~2.8k tokens and completions average ~5.5k; we anticipate ~8k of those per day during month 3 peak.
- 32k usage: not for every request — only for deep historical merges and full account snapshots. Estimate 32k-context requests at ~18% of total generation traffic, but those spikes can be clustered (end of month runs).
- 128k need: exploratory. We have a couple of workflows that might want 128k (complete multi-year transaction histories) but that's <1% initially and could grow.

On pricing: we are comfortable with a blended target of $12/1M tokens for 8k flows, but want a clear uplift schedule for 32k and 128k. Please include options for a committed monthly token tier vs pay-as-you-go.

I will pull together two redacted payload examples and upload to the drive link you shared by EOD today. Also looping Marcus since he'll own procurement.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product Integrations | Fintech Solutions, Inc.
alyssa@fintechsolutions.com
[will upload sample_payloads.json to shared folder]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.dev>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fintechsolutions.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus@fintechsolutions.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.dev>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & context profiling - post-demo recap

Thanks Alyssa — perfect, that level of detail is exactly what we need. Attached is the MAP_v1.xlsx with a proposed timeline (POC -> pilot -> production) and a preliminary pricing slab based on the volumes you called out. Highlights:

- Baseline (8k context)
  - PAYG: $14.00 per 1M tokens
  - Committed tier (>=5M tokens/mo): $11.00 per 1M tokens
- Mid (32k context)
  - PAYG: $28.00 per 1M tokens (2x baseline token-equivalent pricing)
  - Committed tier: $22.00 per 1M tokens
- Long (128k context)
  - PAYG: $60.00 per 1M tokens
  - Committed tier: $48.00 per 1M tokens

Notes on the math: for 32k/128k we price based on effective token cost (execution and memory overhead), not simply a flat multiplier. We also expect to apply caching/prefix reuse for the statement generation flow which typically reduces billable token count by 10-35% depending on reuse. Quantization recommendations and batching can further reduce per-token infer costs (we typically see 15-30% unit-cost reduction with 4-bit quantization on compatible models).

Requested next items from you:
- Upload the two sample payloads to the shared drive (you indicated you would).
- Confirm target commit level you want us to price formally (e.g., 5M/mo vs 10M/mo).
- Agree a date/time for a 60m technical deep-dive (propose Thu 17 Jun 10am PT) so our infra and security SMEs can cover data flows and SOC2 evidence needs.

I've attached the MAP and a blank customer data profile to make the tokenization exercise straightforward. If you want, our team can tokenise your samples and send a short report showing token distribution (prompt vs completion, percent >8k, percent >32k) which I recommend before we lock a commit level.

Links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4521
- Shared drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cMAP_shared

If that all looks good, I'll follow up with a formal pilot quote after we see the samples.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
